programme.title: Europe's Greatest Train Journeys
programme.desc: The Little Yellow Train winds through the Eastern Pyrenees, crossing the Cerdan plateau, the historic Gisclard railway suspension bridge and the Grandes Canalettes caves, known as the underground Versailles of the Pyrenees.

programme.title: Europe's Greatest Train Journeys
programme.desc: Andalusia, now crossed by high-speed and modernized rail lines, unveils its rich culture and landscapes; along the journey, we visit cities like Seville, Granada with its famed Alhambra and Guadix near the Tabernas Desert.

programme.title: Europe's Greatest Train Journeys
programme.desc: In Portugal, in the Douro River Valley, a steam locomotive and a small historic train will take you in turn to the water's edge, on the only railroad line in the world that crosses three World Heritage Sites classified by UNESCO.

programme.title: Europe's Greatest Train Journeys
programme.desc: The Cinque Terre Express runs along Italy's northern coast east of Genoa; passing through five UNESCO-listed villages, it offers coastal views and access to cobbled streets, harbors, terraced vineyards and pastel-colored houses.

programme.title: Europe's Greatest Train Journeys
programme.desc: Corsica, the Island of Beauty, is best explored by railway; from Mediterranean waters to towering peaks, stops include Algajola for a seaside dive, Vizzavona on the GR20 trail and historic cities like Corte with its citadel.

programme.desc: On a mission to taste the world's best breakfast, the three big egos Gordon, Gino and Fred are venturing out of their comfort zones crossing over the USA border into Mexico. They hope to stay out of trouble as they drive their bad boy transporter.

programme.title: Gordon Ramsay's Road Trip
programme.desc: Gordon wants to show Fred & Gino that the food and fresh produce are off the charts! In Las Vegas they indulge in one of the most expensive beef burgers. After a night at the casino they're on the road again to experience the real wild west.

programme.title: Gordon Ramsay's Road Trip
programme.desc: Gino & Fred are excited to head to San Francisco for their very own Summer of Love. Gordon tries to embrace the flower power mood, but he's more interested in the 61 Michelin Stars. The boys travel to a Napa Valley vineyard in a hot air balloon.

programme.title: Gordon Ramsay's Road Trip

programme.sub-title: Best of Salina's Land and Sea

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks Italy

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks Italy
programme.desc: Jamie visits the pizza capital of Italy to learn recipes from the locals and tries acquapazza, fish poached in crazy water.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks Italy

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks Italy

programme.title: George Orwell: A Sage for All Seasons

programme.title: George Orwell: A Sage for All Seasons
programme.sub-title: George Orwell, Child of the British Empire
programme.desc: Orwell's early life as the son of a man who spends his entire life perpetuating the worst evils of the British in the empire's Opium Department pushes young Orwell to learn early on how corrosive lies and omissions are when grace blunts the truth.

programme.title: George Orwell: A Sage for All Seasons
programme.desc: A stubborn sense of English eccentricity takes root in the young George Orwell; the author's childhood in the town of Henley-on-Thames gives Orwell a vision of what he wants to preserve in the face of a 20th century spinning out of control.

programme.title: George Orwell: A Sage for All Seasons
programme.desc: Orwell's school life previews the more ruthless world of oppression he sets down in "Nineteen Eighty-Four", focusing on an ironic essay by Orwell about his time at St. Cyprian's boarding school under the rule of the monstrous bully Mrs. Wilkes.

programme.title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain

programme.title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
programme.sub-title: From Samuel Clemens to Mark Twain
programme.desc: Seeing Twain's life as one of milestones; the financial success brought by his literary triumphs is at times disrupted by disastrous investments such as the Paige typesetting machine; Twain's happy married life is hit by several family tragedies.

programme.title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
programme.sub-title: The Sense of Mark Twain's Humor
programme.desc: Twain says that as a humorist, "I have always preached."; his sermon consists of "cracking up" idols of reverence to make room for truth; his speech about the "cannibals" of the Sandwich Islands shows him tickling the audience's funny bones.

programme.title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
programme.desc: Concerning his writing, Twain once confesses that the motive of profit has an importance "almost beyond my own comprehension."; exploring why money means so much to Twain; detailing the marketing schemes he uses to maximize his income.

programme.title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
programme.desc: Twain's goal in "Innocents Abroad" is to teach his readers to see the Old World with their own eyes, asking what of value can remain after everything is mocked into submission when Twain trains his wit on the holy sites of the Bible.

programme.title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
programme.desc: Twain mines his own past as a prospector and turns it into comic frontier fiction in "Roughing It"; the work also marks Twain's first prominent use of American vernacular language; his intimation that it deserves a place in American literature.
